claims.text: The proposed catalyst is a high-entropy-alloy nanoparticle catalyst.
Combining catalytically active and corrosion-resistant metals in HEA nanoparticles will enhance HER activity relative to conventional Pt-based catalysts.
Combining catalytically active and corrosion-resistant metals in HEA nanoparticles will enhance HOR activity relative to conventional Pt-based catalysts.
The proposed HEA nanoparticles will be more durable than conventional Pt-based catalysts.
The nanoparticles will form a uniform multicomponent solid-solution HEA.
Catalytically active metals can tune hydrogen adsorption and desorption energies in the HEA.
Corrosion-resistant constituent metals can improve the electrochemical corrosion resistance of the HEA nanoparticles.
The intervention will produce a stable, homogeneous, nanoscale solid-solution structure.
A tailored HEA surface composition will balance catalytically active sites with corrosion resistance.
Combinatorial electronic effects among multiple HEA elements will adjust hydrogen adsorption and desorption energies.
The stability of the HEA structure will suppress metal dissolution under harsh electrochemical conditions.
The stability of the HEA structure will suppress surface oxidation under harsh electrochemical conditions.
The HEA catalyst will exhibit lower HER and HOR overpotentials than conventional Pt-based catalysts.
The HEA catalyst will exhibit faster HER and HOR kinetics than conventional Pt-based catalysts.
The HEA catalyst will undergo less performance degradation during extended cycling than conventional Pt-based catalysts.
The expected benefits apply in acidic or alkaline electrolytes under potential cycling and high current densities typical of fuel cells and electrolyzers.
